pl-l4d16c1-d1e115.summary: States that in the perfection of penance three things are to be observed: compunction of heart, confession of mouth, and satisfaction of work.

pl-l4d16c1-d1e118.summary: Quotes Chrysostom: perfect penance makes the sinner bear all things gladly: contrition in his heart, confession in his mouth, all humility in his work; this is fruitful penance, so that as we offend God in three ways, by heart, mouth, and hand, so we satisfy in three ways.
claims: The three parts of penance answer the three ways of sinning.

pl-l4d16c1-d1e127.summary: Quotes Augustine: there are three kinds of sin, in heart, in deed, and in habit or word, like three deaths: one as in the house, when the heart consents to lust; another as carried out of the gate, when consent proceeds to deed; a third when the mind is pressed down by evil habit or armed with harmful self-defense, as already stinking in the tomb. These are the three kinds of dead the Lord raised.
claims: Sin in heart, deed, and habit are three deaths.
They correspond to the three dead raised by Christ.

pl-l4d16c1-d1e140.summary: Concludes that this threefold death is met by a threefold remedy: contrition, confession, satisfaction.
claims: Contrition, confession, and satisfaction heal the three deaths.

pl-l4d16c1-d1e143.summary: Shows compunction commended in 'rend your hearts and not your garments'.

pl-l4d16c1-d1e149.summary: Shows confession commended in 'the just man is first accuser of himself', since he truly confesses who accuses himself and imputes evil to himself; and in 'pour out your hearts before him' and 'confess your sins to one another'.

pl-l4d16c1.summary: Sets out the three parts of perfect penance: compunction of heart, confession of mouth, and satisfaction of work. Chrysostom: as we offend God in three ways, by heart, mouth, and deed, so we satisfy in three ways. Augustine's three kinds of sin, in heart, deed, and habit, are like the three dead whom the Lord raised, in the house, carried out of the gate, and stinking in the tomb; these three deaths are met by the threefold remedy of contrition, confession, and satisfaction. Scripture commends compunction ('rend your hearts') and confession ('the just accuses himself first').
claims: Perfect penance has three parts: contrition, confession, and satisfaction.
They answer the three ways we offend God: heart, mouth, and deed.
The three kinds of sin are like the three dead raised by Christ.
